title: Epimorphic compatible-pair maps detect quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $P,X$ be integer-indexed cochain complexes, and let $a:P\to X$ be a chain map [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $Z^n(K)=\ker(d_K^n:K^n\to K^{n+1})$, $z^n:Z^n(P)\to Z^n(X)$ for the map induced by $a$, and $\bar d_K^n:K^n\to Z^{n+1}(K)$ for the differential with codomain restricted to cycles. For each $n\in\mathbf Z$ form the pullback
$$T^n=X^n\times_{Z^{n+1}(X)}Z^{n+1}(P)$$
using $\bar d_X^n$ and $z^{n+1}$. The chain-map identity defines $e^n=(a^n,\bar d_P^n):P^n\to T^n$. Suppose every $e^n$ is an epimorphism. Then every $a^n$ and every $z^n$ is an epimorphism, and every $H^n(a):H^n(P)\to H^n(X)$ is an isomorphism. Thus $a$ is a degreewise epimorphic quasi-isomorphism. No boundedness, projectivity, or existence of projective covers is assumed.

proof.text: Use ordinary composition notation, so $fg=f\circ g$. Fix $n$. For an object $B$ and maps $y:B\to X^n$, $x:B\to Z^{n+1}(P)$ satisfying $\bar d_X^n y=z^{n+1}x$, the pullback property gives $(y,x):B\to T^n$. Apply clause (a) of [lem-sp-abelian-refinements] to the epimorphism $e^n$: there are an epimorphism $p:B'\to B$ and $u:B'\to P^n$ with $a^n u=yp$ and $\bar d_P^n u=xp$. This is simultaneous lifting after an epimorphic refinement, not lifting on $\operatorname{Hom}(B,-)$ itself.

proof.text: Given $y:B\to Z^n(X)$, compose with the cycle inclusion and use Step 1 with the compatible pair $(y,0)$ in degree $n$. The resulting $u$ satisfies $\bar d_P^n u=0$, hence factors uniquely through $Z^n(P)$. Its image under $z^n$ equals $yp$, by cancellation of the cycle inclusion of $X$. Clause (a) of [lem-sp-abelian-refinements] now shows that $z^n$ is epic, for every $n$.

proof.text: Given $y:B\to X^n$, apply clause (a) of [lem-sp-abelian-refinements] to the epic $z^{n+1}$ and $\bar d_X^n y$. Obtain an epimorphism $p:B'\to B$ and $x:B'\to Z^{n+1}(P)$ with $z^{n+1}x=\bar d_X^n yp$. Step 1 applied to $(yp,x)$ gives a further epimorphism $p':B''\to B'$ and $u:B''\to P^n$ with $a^n u=ypp'$. The composite $pp'$ is epic: cancellation first through $p'$ and then through $p$ proves this directly. Clause (a) therefore shows that $a^n$ is epic for every $n$.

proof.text: Write $q_K:Z^n(K)\to H^n(K)$ for the quotient by $\operatorname{im}\bar d_K^{n-1}$, using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This quotient is a cokernel of $\bar d_K^{n-1}$: a morphism killing $\bar d_K^{n-1}$ kills its image, and then factors uniquely through the quotient. In particular $q_K$ is epic, since two maps equal after $q_K$ are the same factorization. The chain-map identity and functoriality give $z^n\bar d_P^{n-1}=\bar d_X^{n-1}a^{n-1}$ and $H^n(a)q_P=q_Xz^n$.

proof.text: Let $k:L\to Z^n(P)$ be the kernel of $z^n$. The pair $(0,k):L\to T^{n-1}$ is compatible. Step 1 gives an epimorphism $p:L'\to L$ and $u:L'\to P^{n-1}$ with $\bar d_P^{n-1}u=kp$ and $a^{n-1}u=0$. Thus $q_Pkp=q_P\bar d_P^{n-1}u=0$; cancellation of $p$ gives $q_Pk=0$. The complex $L\xrightarrow{k}Z^n(P)\xrightarrow{z^n}Z^n(X)$ is exact in the middle, since $k$ is the kernel inclusion, whose image is itself. Its second arrow is epic by Step 2. Clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] makes $z^n$ a cokernel of $k$. Consequently there is a unique $g:Z^n(X)\to H^n(P)$ with $gz^n=q_P$.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution (1), verification of IH_{n-1}; general compatible-pair criterion extracted from this verification, without boundedness. See also Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist (3).

proof.text: The identities of Steps 4--5 give $g\bar d_X^{n-1}a^{n-1}=gz^n\bar d_P^{n-1}=q_P\bar d_P^{n-1}=0$. Cancel the epic $a^{n-1}$ of Step 3. Since $q_X$ is the cokernel of $\bar d_X^{n-1}$, obtain $h:H^n(X)\to H^n(P)$ with $hq_X=g$. Then $hH^n(a)q_P=hq_Xz^n=gz^n=q_P$, so $hH^n(a)=1$ by cancellation of $q_P$. Also $H^n(a)hq_Xz^n=H^n(a)q_P=q_Xz^n$; cancel $z^n$ and $q_X$ to get $H^n(a)h=1$. Thus every $H^n(a)$ is an isomorphism. Together with Step 3 and the definition of quasi-isomorphism in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], this proves the assertion. No step starts an induction at an upper bound.
